script.name: t_h1_gateway_bad_input
script.objective: [H1] Start gateway-rs. On three separate connections send an empty body, a 64 KiB header and a body with invalid UTF-8 bytes (0xff 0xfe); after each, a valid request on a new connection. FAIL (H1:proven) if the gateway exits or a valid request gets no reply; the exit code, the HTTP status of each valid request and of each bad request are recorded. PASS (H1:disproved) if every valid request is answered. A port closed after 10 s is a SETUP fault.

script.name: t_h2_go_slow_client
script.objective: [H2] Start service-go, send a request without the final blank line and measure how long the server holds the socket, up to 60 s. FAIL (H2:proven) if it is still held at 60 s; PASS (H2:disproved) with the time otherwise. Then 200 such sockets are opened and a valid request on a new one is timed against 5 s (recorded).

script.name: t_h3_cs_swallowed_error
script.objective: [H3] Start service-cs with its backend (gateway-rs) not running and send the request that reaches the backend call. FAIL (H3:proven) on a 2xx, with status and body recorded; PASS (H3:disproved) on 4xx/5xx. Control: with the backend up the same request must give 2xx.

script.name: t_h4_binscan_netexpose_egress
script.objective: [H4] tapi_binscan on gateway-rs, service-go, service-cs, cpp-demo and libpycore.so (NX, PIE, RELRO, canary; canary only noted for C#), tapi_netexpose with all three services running (only the three contract ports allowed), tapi_egress with only 127.0.0.1 on those ports allowed. All results go to one tapi_cybersec_report; FAIL (H4:proven) on the first finding, naming the file and the flag. A scanner that returns no data at all gives INCONCLUSIVE, naming the scanner.
